thread:
customer_julia: Hey team — after upgrading @redwood/sdk-node to 2.3.0 our Next.js app on Vercel (edge runtime) started failing with CORS preflight 401s when the SDK call relies on cookie auth. Works locally, only in Vercel deploy. Anyone seen this?

support_aly: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste minimal repro + the error response body? 401 on OPTIONS or on the POST?

customer_julia: OPTIONS returns 401. POST sometimes 200 if I retry from the browser. Quick repro: client in an edge route does a fetch to our api proxy which forwards to Redwood hosted API. We rely on a session cookie set on the browser. Locally (next dev) preflight succeeds. On vercel edge the preflight returns 401 and browser stops.

customer_julia: Code snippet (simplified):
```
// edge handler in /api/gen/edge.ts
import { EdgeRuntimeClient } from '@redwood/sdk-node'
export default async (req) => {
  const c = new EdgeRuntimeClient({ auth: 'cookie' })
  return c.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
}
```

devex_sam: Two quick guesses: 1) Vercel edge may be treating the preflight as a separate request without cookies (so your upstream sees no session and rejects), 2) SDK 2.3.0 changed how it forwards credentials in the edge bundle. Which exact SDK package/version did you upgrade from?

customer_julia: We upgraded from 2.1.7 -> 2.3.0. I also noticed an extra header X-Forwarded-Host present in vercel but not locally.

eng-runtime-tim: If OPTIONS is hitting your proxy and returning 401, that's an app-level auth check firing on preflight. Preflight must be allowed through without auth (CORS preflight should return 200 + appropriate Access-Control-Allow-* headers). Can you share the proxy handler?

customer_julia: Proxy is basically: verify session cookie, then proxy request to api.redwood.example.com (internal). We didn't special-case OPTIONS.

support_aly: That explains it — OPTIONS should not require session. Quick mitigation: return 200 for OPTIONS and include:
``nAccess-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin>
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization,Content-Type
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,OPTIONS
```
Also ensure your browser fetch from the page includes credentials: `fetch(url, { credentials: 'include' })` or set the SDK option that toggles fetch credentials.

devex_sam: Note re: SDK 2.3.0: we shipped a small change where the edge bundle uses a platform fetch wrapper that omits credentials by default to avoid leaking cookies across SSR boundaries. If your app relied on implicit cookies, you need to pass { credentials: 'include' } into the EdgeRuntimeClient or set REDWOOD_EDGE_INCLUDE_CREDENTIALS=true in env for now. We're shipping a patch to make this explicit in the docs.

customer_julia: Ah — how do I pass credentials in the new client API? I don't see it in the types.

devex_sam: Use the low-level fetchOverride option for now:
```
new EdgeRuntimeClient({ fetchOverride: (url, opts={}) => fetch(url, { ...opts, credentials: 'include' }) })
```
That should attach cookies for preflight and actual request.

eng-runtime-tim: Also check Vercel's docs: if the edge function is invoked cross-origin, the browser sends preflight from the origin to your edge function. The edge must not attempt to validate session on OPTIONS — simply return the CORS headers. After that the actual POST will include cookies if `credentials: 'include'` is set.

customer_julia: Thanks — I added the fetchOverride and special-cased OPTIONS to 200/headers. Preflight passes now but I'm still seeing occasional 401s on POST (racey). Any ideas?

support_aly: Can you share request/response headers of the failing POST? Often a mismatch between cookie domain/path or SameSite attribute will cause cookies to be omitted in edge contexts. Vercel's platform can alter hostnames so domain scoping matters.

customer_julia: Here's a failing POST headers excerpt (sanitized):
``
Request: Origin: https://app.example.com
Cookie: session=abcd1234
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 ...

Response: status 401
WWW-Authenticate: Session expired
```

eng-runtime-tim: That suggests upstream session store considered the session invalid; could be a timing/clock skew if tokens are short-lived, or a load-balancer sticky session miss. Are you using signed cookies + a KMS? Any recent key rotation?

customer_julia: We're on signed cookies, and we did a key rotation last week but rolled-forward. Some users hit 401 then can retry successfully. 2.1.7 didn't show this pattern.

devex_sam: Two more things to try: 1) Enable SDK retries to hide transient auth flakiness (temporary workaround) — EdgeRuntimeClient accepts retry config in 2.3.0 as `retries: { retries: 2, factor: 1 }`. 2) Capture full request IDs and correlate with backend logs to see why session lookup failed. If key rotation is implicated, look for signature verification errors.

customer_julia: Ok setting retries + logging. If we confirm it's a key rotation / signature verify failure we'll revert rotation and coordinate.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished for app/example-site (commit c3f5a9) — environment REDWOOD_EDGE_INCLUDE_CREDENTIALS=true applied to preview.

support_aly: Thanks — please paste the backend log correlation once you have it and we can follow up. If this repros consistently we can open an internal bug for the SDK behavior around credentials and default preflight handling. :thumbsup:

customer_julia: Will do — thanks for the quick help!
